      "observations": [
        "Read all seventeen owned Rust paths and all 944 diff lines. The patch introduces a crate-private ServerType helper trait with a blanket implementation for AuthenticationProvider + UserInteractiveServer + RefCounted, then replaces repeated equivalent written triples in operation methods, implementations and copy/move builders. Imports are adjusted accordingly.",
        "The original client struct retains RefCounted + static, and its constructor impl uses ServerType + static. The helper trait itself adds no lifetime bound or methods. This is a named supertrait bundle with a blanket implementation, not a runtime wrapper or a claim about object safety, Send/Sync or protocol ABI.",
        "The two unchanged construct_request helpers retain the narrower RefCounted-only server constraint, so their RefCounted imports stay. Other operation/request-type bounds and PhantomData roles are not replaced by ServerType. The most common wording in the new comment is narrower than every server generic.",
        "Current accepted code moves ServerType into protocol_shared and adds PrefBasedServer; current EWS imports that shared bundle and keeps static explicit. The shared DoOperation is now generic over Client and Err. Those later changes are not credited to this EWS-local three-bound patch.",
        "Owned hunks change bounds, imports and the new helper declaration, not request construction branches or listener-success/error bodies. The custom read-status handling remains a distinct operation behavior. No test or assertion changes; no Rust compile, Clippy, runtime request or behavior-equivalence result is claimed.",
        "Manual naming/style is scoped to these Rust generic roles. ServerT, RequestT and OperationDataT continue to name different parameters, and crate-private visibility is explicit. This is an accepted local shorthand, not a global requirement to invent aggregate traits or replace narrower constraints.",
        "Reuse the exact original B complete Bug 1982671 description/comments 0–27/end from the prior family audit. The large family discussion is not reread or credited as a new capture.",
